mentions.name: Hale
mentions.description: An abstract distributed systems programming language that offers fine-grained control over resources while requiring programmers to agree with the compiler on resource intent. Programs situate computations within a recursive graph structure incorporating message broker semantics, giving the compiler a unified view across arbitrary process boundaries. It supports effects and formal verification syntax so architectural decisions are checked by the compiler, and its infrastructure-aware compiler can configure the environments applications deploy to, handling everything from individual memory allocations to distributed fleet deployments. The language is close to v1.
